intro: ISRD, Interdisciplinary Systems R&D, does applied interdisciplinary systems research and design. We take what the systems sciences and the sciences of each field already know, apply it to real problems, build tools for the people doing the changing, and find out in public whether the tools work.

what.title: Tools for systemic change
what.text: A suite of tools for people who help others change a system: models to run, a studio to think and write in, and more to come.

what.title: Start here
what.text: A plain guide to how systems work, from everyday examples, with no background needed.

what.title: Research
what.text: Do tools for systemic change work? Our questions, methods and commitments, with the papers behind them.

what.title: Projects and community
what.text: Issue projects led by the people closest to each issue, and a community of people who use and improve the tools.

principles_intro: What we promise, and what we do not do.

principles.title: People stay in charge
principles.text: The AI proposes and you decide. Consequential decisions stay with the people making them.

principles.title: Sketches are labelled
principles.text: AI text meant for the page is called a sketch, kept apart from yours, and meant to be tested and rewritten.

principles.title: We say how sure we are
principles.text: Every claim is a known pattern, a likely parallel, or a guess worth testing.

principles.title: We publish what we find
principles.text: Whatever it shows. We build on existing systems science and put it to work.

principles.title: Customers publish their own work
principles.text: Customers publish under their own names, and ISRD provides the tools.

mission: AI can give everybody a voice: a say in how Earth's resources are managed and where our civilization goes next. ISRD aims to help many producers, especially people who need AI support to be heard, and to keep the picture pluralistic: many perspectives, understood together.

person.name: Kurt Rowley, PhD
person.title: Systems scientist · Health researcher · Instructional designer
person.bio: Kurt develops a rigorous, non-linear methodology for understanding complex adaptive systems, from post-viral illness to civilizational dynamics to the craft of writing. The work draws on general systems theory, cybernetics, complexity science and design-based research, and builds on decades of research in instructional design and learning technology.
person.collab: ISRD welcomes collaboration with researchers and organizations on specific projects where the fit is right.

aim: Our aim is a civilization where everybody has a voice in how Earth's resources are managed and where we go next. AI can help many producers, and the people who need it most, be heard, so the picture stays pluralistic: many perspectives, understood together.
